transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-24
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Liu (Redwood Product), Lena Ortiz (Harbor Analytics - Head of ML), Tom Reeves (Harbor - Infra Lead), Priya Nair (Harbor - CTO)

Summary:
Quick Optimize walkthrough focusing on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8), quality vs latency tradeoffs for Harbor's chat & summarization workloads, and next steps for a short pilot/benchmark. Customer concerned about latency SLOs for interactive product and data residency/SOC2 compliance.

Topics:
- INT8 vs FP8 general tradeoffs
- Redwood Optimize tooling: profiling, recommended quant profiles
- Expected quality regressions and how we measure/regress
- Dedicated vs hosted routing for latency guarantees
- Benchmarks to run for pilot

Questions noted:
- How much quality drop with INT8 on our models?
- Do you support mixed-precision per-layer profiles?
- Can we run FP8 on dedicated instances and fall back to INT8 if capacity tight?

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros, I'm Sofia AE on the Redwood platform and with me is Ethan and Maya from SE/product — Ethan do you want to kick off the Optimize walkthrough?
[00:18] Ethan (Redwood SE): Yeah thanks Sofia. Hi Lena, Tom, Priya. We'll go through quant profiles, some live console demos in Optimize, then a quality vs latency example. Note transcription maybe a little fuzzy on model names.
[00:30] Lena (Harbor): Great, thanks. Our main things: interactive chat latency target is p95 <= 250ms, and summarization batch jobs can be slower but quality important. We currently run on a mix of M40-ish VMs and some managed endpoints.
[00:48] Tom (Harbor Infra): For security, SOC2 is a must, also where'd the data rest with Hosted — we need audit logs and KMS support.
[01:05] Sofia: Totally — Hosted supports KMS integrations, audit logs, and for Dedicated/Private we do VPC options. We'll share the SOC2 docs after.
[01:20] Ethan: Ok jumping in — first, what is quantization profile? It's basically per-layer config that says which parts of the network we run at INT8 vs FP16 or FP8. On some models INT8 gives huge throughput wins; on others FP8 is a better quality-latency sweet spot.
[01:43] Maya (Product): In Optimize you'll see a guided profiler that runs a few sample prompts and suggests profiles: safe-int8, aggressive-int8, fp8-mixed. It surfaces predicted token-level latency and a small quality delta estimate.
[02:05] Priya (Harbor): How reliable are the quality deltas? We can't have hallucination regressions for customer-facing summaries.
[02:16] Ethan: Good question — we measure on your holdout prompts and run an eval set. The tool gives BLEU/ROUGE style deltas and also human-annotated regression flags if you want. It's an estimate; we always recommend a short human eval for critical flows.
[02:35] Lena: Can we do per-route profiles? Chat route needs stricter latency, summarization can be more aggressive.
[02:44] Ethan: Yes — routing supports per-route quant profiles and automatic fallback. You can pin a model+profile to a route in the Console.
[03:02] [demo noise — Ethan sharing screen, console UI clicks] Ethan: Here's Optimize runbook — I'll run a quick profile for a 7B chat model using Harbor's sample prompts (we used a representative prompt set).
[03:20] [03:20] Ethan: Running profiler... it runs short microbenchmarks and a small quality pass. Outcome: safe-int8 yields ~2.8x throughput improvement, p95 token latency improved from 110ms to 45ms per token, but quality delta shows ~0.9% ROUGE drop on the summarization set. fp8-mixed shows 2.3x throughput with 0.2% ROUGE drop.
[03:52] Tom: Those numbers look promising for chat. Is the p95 latency you reported end-to-end or just token generation?
[04:00] Ethan: That was model inference token latency; end-to-end will add network and prep time — but with Dedicated we can get closer to those numbers.
[04:12] Priya: So INT8 has bigger perf but more quality risk; FP8 safer. Can we do hybrid profiles, e.g., INT8 for earlier layers FP8 for attention?
[04:24] Ethan: Absolutely — Optimize supports mixed precision per-layer. The profiler sometimes recommends mixed profiles when it sees sensitivity in specific layers.
[04:37] Lena: For our customer chat we need p95 <=250ms. With safe-int8 you quoted token numbers that look ok — what's typical end-to-end on Dedicated?
[04:48] Ethan: On Dedicated GPU pools with NVLink-ish networking we often hit end-to-end p95 180-220ms for interactive 2-turn chats at 2k context, depends on batching. We'll also show batching knobs in Console.
[05:06] Sofia: On pricing note — INT8 aggressive can reduce token compute cost by ~40-60% depending on model; FP8 reduces ~30-45%. We'll include model-specific cost delta in the pricing sheet.
[05:24] [05:24] Ethan: Quick note, sometimes profiler mislabels the architecture names in the exported notes — it's auto transcribed, so just a heads up.
[05:35] Tom: For compliance — if we run Dedicated in our cloud region can we still have KMS key control?
[05:43] Maya: Yes, Dedicated and Private allow customer-managed keys and full audit logging.
[05:50] Lena: If we do a pilot, what's the measurement plan? We want to benchmark p95 latency, throughput, and summary quality with human eval.
[05:58] Ethan: Suggested plan: 1) You share 1k sample prompts and expected p95 target; 2) We run profiler and baseline measurements on your sample; 3) We produce a suggested quant profile + estimated cost savings and run small human evals on top. That matches the next steps we noted.
[06:18] [demo continued — console shows perf graphs] Ethan: Here you can toggle quant profiles and run side-by-side compare. You can also schedule nightly jobs to re-profile as your distribution changes.
[06:35] Priya: What about fallback policies? If FP8 capacity is exhausted can we fallback to INT8 or FP16?
[06:44] Ethan: Yes you can set fallback chains — e.g., try FP8 on high-performance pool, if not available route to safe-int8 or hosted FP16. Redwood handles automated routing based on policies you set.
[07:00] Tom: Network jitter is our fear — is there ability to pin to local region and restrict cross-region?
[07:07] Sofia: You can pin model deployments to a region and also use VPC peering for Dedicated; network topology and egress can be configured in Private deployments as well.
[07:20] Lena: Any examples of hallucination regressions from INT8?
[07:28] Ethan: On some creative-generation workloads we see slight decoding artifacts; for summarization, regression is usually small but non-zero — that's why we recommend the human eval gate. Also Optimize can auto-generate counterexamples if it detects divergence.
[07:45] [08:00] Customer Q&A and edge cases — interruptions and clarifications; some transcription garble: 'K-V cash' for KV cache, 'eff pee eight' for FP8
[10:12] Ethan: We'll share the benchmark sheet — it has columns for model, profile, throughput, p50/p95, quality delta, and notes. Use that to pick the profile you want to pilot.
[12:30] Priya: How do we integrate with our CI for model rollouts and canarying?
[12:40] Maya: Console supports rollouts, canaries, and automatic rollback policies; Optimize ties into that so you can promote a profile after a successful eval.
[13:05] Lena: Any limitations on mixed precision per-layer for very large models 70B+?
[13:13] Ethan: For 70B+ it depends on the hardware and quant kernels. Some kernels still need FP16 for some attention math. Optimize will flag unsupported combos.
[13:30] Tom: On the pilot — we want Dedicated test with FP8 mixed and an INT8 aggressive comparison. How long to spin up a Dedicated test pool?
[13:40] Sofia: We can provision a small Dedicated pool for pilot in ~3-5 business days once contract and capacity are agreed. For immediate tests we can run hosted instances but with less strict SLO.
[14:00] [14:00] Ethan runs a quick quality-vs-latency chart showing curves — FP8 sits to the left of INT8 (less latency cost) but tradeoff depends on model/data.
[15:05] Lena: Are there best practices for prompt engineering to keep quantization stable?
[15:12] Ethan: Yes shorter prompts and fewer rare tokens reduce sensitivity; we also recommend context truncation and prefix caching which Optimize automates.
[16:00] [16:00] Small digression on billing: per-token compute differences, rounding, and credits for pilot usage.
[18:20] Priya: Any competitors we should worry about — who does this similarly?
[18:28] Sofia: A few — managed providers mention simple endpoints; some teams roll their own Triton + quant stacks, but Redwood focuses on production tooling + observability around quant profiles.
[19:00] Tom: For security review we'll need SOC2, HIPAA (if needed), and network diagrams.
[19:08] Sofia: We'll attach SOC2 and network diagrams to the follow-up email.
[19:20] [19:20] Action items recap by Sofia:
- Sofia to send pilot pricing and reserved capacity options (due 2026-06-28)
- Ethan to share quantization runbook and benchmark sheet (due 2026-06-26)
- Lena to provide 1k sample prompts and target p95 (due 2026-07-02)

[19:50] Priya: What's the success criteria for the pilot?
[19:55] Lena: Meet p95 <= 250ms for chat with <=1% quality regression vs baseline on our human eval.
[20:05] Sofia: Good, we'll align scope for a 2-week pilot to validate both latency and quality.

[20:15] [closing minutes — logistical Q&A about contract and timeline]
[22:00] Sofia: Any more technical blockers we didn't cover?
[22:05] Tom: Just a note — we'll need some compliance questions answered by legal; can you route those to our procurement contact?
[22:12] Sofia: Yes we'll include legal and procurement docs.

[23:00] Final wrap and thanks.
